also: he didn’t beat around the bush

terms.gloss: beat around the bush, talk round a thing
evidence: Ter. And. 1.2.31: nīl circuitiōne ūsus es (Lewis & Short s.v. circuitiō)
terms.comment: Circumitiō (or circuitiō) is a going round; ūtī takes the ablative. “Don’t beat around the bush” is nōlī circumitiōne ūtī.

phrases.latin: quid opus est circumitiōne et anfractū?
phrases.english: what need is there for going round and round?
He didn’t beat around the bush.

sources: Lewis & Short: circuitio · Lewis & Short: utor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 93, 94.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
